text: Every AI app I try asks me the same things. What I eat. Where I fly from.
I want to say it once, and have it follow me, without any company holding it for me.
This is Pip, an AI assistant. One touch of my passkey, the fingerprint or face unlock my phone already uses, and my memory vault is open.
I tell Pip I'm vegetarian. Pip picks out the fact and locks it right here in the browser, with a key only my passkey can make.
Then: I fly out of B L R. Same thing.
cap: Then: I fly out of BLR. Same thing.

text: What gets stored is scrambled. No fact is readable anywhere outside this tab.
Now Fern, a different AI app with its own key. It sees nothing about me.
Fern asks for access, and Pip asks me.
Saying yes is a transaction on Monad, so it needs a small network fee. I top up from the faucet.
Allow. That writes a grant to Monad: a permission slip any app can check and no app can fake.
Only the permission slip goes on chain. The memories themselves stay locked in my browser.
Fern opens both memories with its own key. It never touched my passkey.
I ask it to plan my weekend. Vegetarian food, a flight out of Bangalore. It never asks me a thing.
Now I change my mind. One tap, one more transaction.
Pip locks every memory again, with a brand new key. Fern's permission slip only fits the old one.
Fern still holds its slip. I go back and ask again. Every memory is locked.
The plan comes back generic. Fern didn't promise to forget. It can't open my memories any more.
Straight from the chain: both transactions succeeded, and the version number of the lock went from one to two. Nothing in between that I have to trust.
For developers, it's one package: npm install satchel S D K. Lock, grant, revoke. The code on the page is the code that runs.
cap: For developers, it's one package: npm install satchel-sdk. Lock, grant, revoke. The code on the page is the code that runs.

text: My AI's memory follows me to any app I allow, and one tap takes it back. Pip, Fern and the S D K are live at satchel dash keys dot ver sell dot app.
